items.title: Zendaya, EmRata, & More It Girls Are Already Obsessed With Fall's Top Boot Trends
items.description: This Season’s Buzziest Boot Trends Serve Effortless It-Girl Energy
items.author: Alyssa Lapid
paragraphs: This Season’s Buzziest Boot Trends Serve Effortless It-Girl Energy
Zendaya, EmRata, and Anne Hathaway have already mapped out the playbook for your fall footwear.

Thank the fashion gods: Boot season is finally here. And if your favorite style stars are any indication, the vibe this fall is about the perfect mix of high-drama statements and wearable walk-everywhere shoes. Instead of running the same plain pairs into the ground, the girlies have been swapping them out for footwear that feels a bit sharper and instantly put-together.

Right now, over-the-knee boots are dominating the FYPs. From ultra-loose, slouchy styles to super-fitted, second-skin options, the Anne Hathaway-approved thigh-highs are a chic way to keep wearing minidresses even in the cooler months. Lace-ups are another fave, serving Victorian-era-heroine-meets-modern-cool-girl realness. Then there’s the knife-sharp pointed toe — while it might require a bit of dedication to pull off, it comes in so many options that it’s almost a disservice to your ‘fit to *not* wear it out.

Whether you’re headed to a fancy event or simply off to a pumpkin spice latte run, consider this your sign to lace up, zip up, and strut in this season’s chicest pairs. Your fall wardrobe depends on it.

Lace-up boots are nothing new — combat boots are basically a rite of passage at this point. But this season’s lace-up pairs are trading their classic rock roots for something a little more steampunk-meets-vixen. They come in sleek pointed-toe styles, sky-high platforms, or with lots of metal hardware that practically sparkles. Cynthia Erivo already gave them the red-carpet treatment, while Rosalía wore custom Miista pairs for her LUX Tour (now available to shop in a limited-edition run).

These are surprisingly easy to style, whether you want to lean into a punk look or go a bit more balletcore. The lace-up details aren’t limited to the front, either — look out for subtle side corsetry or ties along the back for a completely unexpected twist.

For anyone who is completely over towering high heels, the latest runway shifts are a welcome relief. Kitten heels have been trending for a hot minute, and they’ve finally made their way onto boots. The Fall/Winter 2026 runways of Prada, Ferragamo, and Celine proved that pretty much every silhouette is getting the low-heel treatment — think knee-high, ankle, slouchy, and embroidered options in just about every color imaginable.

Unlike their stiletto sisters, these are much more comfortable, allowing you to take them from your 9-to-5 to after-work drinks. Beyond the usual skinny heel, low cone shapes are also getting a ton of love among the style set. Emily Ratajkowski, for one, is already sold.

Nothing screams “I’m a baddie” more than over-the-knee boots. Everyone from Hollywood actors to pop stars is embracing the tall style, which made a splash on the Fall/Winter 2026 runways of Balenciaga, Chloé, Stella McCartney, and Valentino.

But don’t be intimidated by the height. The key is to play with proportions. While they pair well with a range of styles, these confidence boosters really shine with teeny tiny skirts or dresses. Hathaway’s billowy ruffled minidress paired perfectly well with her second-skin suede boots. Commit to the boot and own the drama.

A sharp pointed-toe boot is classic for a reason: It instantly makes an outfit more polished and fashion girl-coded. This season, the elongated silhouette gets a fresh spin with equestrian-inspired details, satin finishes, and unexpected textures. Basically, there’s a sharp boot for every aesthetic.
Need inspo? Pair them with a dress to allow the footwear to take center stage like Bella Hadid, or let their pointy ends peek under loose jeans for a more low-key touch.
You don’t need to own a bike to hop on the moto boot trend. The shoe — typically characterized by chunky lug soles and heavy metal accents — is enough to give any outfit an instant edge.

For an easy styling route, try pairing a buckle-clad set with your off-duty jeans-and-T-shirt combo. You can also opt for a chunky-soled pair like Zendaya and rock it with low-key utilitarian pieces for that effortless cool-girl vibe. Too hard-edged? There are pairs in lighter colors or with bedazzled buckles if you want to soften up the look.

items.title: Even Sue Bird Is A Fan Of This WNBA-Inspired Art Account
items.description: Meg, 36, is living a bit of a double life. She works full-time in health care by day, but online, she’s known as Thee W Artíste, aka @wnbaart. She started her account in May and now has about 110,000 followers across Instagram and Threads. Her googly-eyed cart
items.author: Alexis Morillo
paragraphs: Meg, 36, is living a bit of a double life. She works full-time in health care by day, but online, she’s known as Thee W Artíste, aka @wnbaart. She started her account in May and now has about 110,000 followers across Instagram and Threads. Her googly-eyed cartoons of viral WNBA moments have carved out her niche among the league’s supporters. And although her online persona is only six months old, Meg has been a fan of the WNBA for decades.

She was in elementary school when the league started in 1996, but it wasn’t until her home state got its own team, the Chicago Sky, in 2006 that she became, in her words, “obsessed with the W.” Meg has loved basketball and art for as long as she can remember (“I was the girl that was always drawing or painting”) and began to combine her passions ahead of the 2026 WNBA season.

“We had just signed that new CBA agreement. I was so excited for all the team mix-ups, with players on different teams now. And I just started drawing cartoons for fun at bedtime,” she tells Bustle. When she started to share her work online, she had no expectations that people would actually engage with it. Her initial idea was to draw graphics about the matchups for the day or the big stories of the league, but she quickly realized what followers reacted to most: whimsy.
“[My art] went in this really niche direction of just trying to find moments in the game that were silly or funny and brought joy to so many people,” she says.

Her account really began to gain traction on June 17, when she posted her drawing of Natasha Cloud doing her “pride celly.” In July, basketball legend Sue Bird shouted out the @wnbaart account on her podcast, and Meg’s follower count has been growing steadily ever since.

When Meg attended WNBA All-Star Weekend this year, she says she was treated like a celebrity. “I was so unprepared and so overwhelmed by the amount of in-person love that I got,” she says. “I was approached constantly for autographs and pictures. It’s so fun that every WNBA event I go to now, I have built-in friends.”

Now after every game her mentions on Threads and Instagram are flooded with comments from fans telling her about “The Moment” from that matchup that needs to be drawn. Sometimes she can whip up a cartoon in 10 minutes; other times it takes hours.
Ahead of the WNBA Finals, Bustle caught up with Meg, Thee W Artíste, to hear about her online habits, her go-to catchphrase, and the unexpected thing that made her cry recently.
The Fast Follow With @WNBAArt
What’s the weirdest internet rabbit hole you’ve gone down recently?

I was thinking about George Washington and looked up what his accent may have sounded like at that time. Was it a British accent? I started questioning what he may have sounded like and what other people in that area at that time sounded like. We don’t have videos of them speaking, so I had to look it up to try and find out!
What app do you rack up the most screen time on?
It used to be Instagram, but after this past summer it has shifted to Threads. WNBA Threads, if you’re in it, is a great community.
What have you been listening to lately?
I’m really excited about the next season of Bridgerton. So sometimes I’ll just listen to the string quartet versions of songs and then try to imagine where they would work well in the next season.
What’s your most used motto?

Six years ago my psychiatrist said, “A bad day does not equal a bad week. A bad week does not equal a bad month. A bad month does not equal a bad year. A bad year does not equal a bad life.” Whenever I’m going through something hard, I remind myself of this. At any given moment things can really turn around for you, which really has been this entire year for me.
What’s the weirdest thing you’ve cried at recently?
I cried watching someone react to a Glee episode last night. Embarrassing on so many levels.
This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

items.title: The Stars Of ‘Paranormal Activity’ Love “Scaring The Sh*t Out Of People”
items.description: The Stars Of Paranormal Activity Love “Scaring The Sh*t Out Of People”
items.author: Christina Amoroso
paragraphs: The Stars Of Paranormal Activity Love “Scaring The Sh*t Out Of People”
Travis A. Knight and Cher Álvarez are making their Broadway debuts in a new play filled with jump scares, and having a blast doing so — even though only one of them is a horror fan.

Broadway’s new thriller Paranormal Activity is the rare theatrical experience in which being surrounded by an audience that shrieks, gasps, and jumps in the middle of a scene doesn’t annoy — it adds to the fun. And its stars, Travis A. Knight and Cher Álvarez, love it. “I fear for my next theater contract because I’m going to be like, ‘Why aren’t you guys reacting?’” says Álvarez. “We love scaring the sh*t out of people.”
“When I put the flashlight on the shower curtain… some guy yelled, ‘Do it,’ as I was about to pull it open,” adds Knight of a recent show. “I was like, ‘I got you, bro. I’m about to do it.’”

Though it lives within the Paranormal Activity universe, Levi Holloway’s play, recently extended through Feb. 28 at the August Wilson Theatre, follows an entirely original plot: A young American couple, Jimmy and Lou (Knight and Álvarez, who shine in their Broadway debuts), have moved to London from Chicago in an effort to put some unsettling experiences behind them. But they, and the audience, soon discover the terror has followed them and is more intense than ever. As the show’s tagline goes, “Places aren’t haunted; people are.”

The excellent performances, sharp writing, inventive direction, and spooky sound and lighting add up to compelling theater, but the production’s unique — and jolting — dimension is the collective reaction of the audience. Along with 1,200 other people, you’ll find yourself gripped by fear one minute, laughing with relief the next. But don’t get too comfortable; the jump scares keep coming.
“It’s a f*cking riot,” says Álvarez. “It’s so dope that horror actually works onstage.”

Álvarez: You’ve got to keep it light. Our dressing rooms are on the same floor, so we’re f*cking with each other all the time, trying to scare each other. Music is also such a way in for me. I think what gets the most exciting is wondering, “What is going to be the personality of this audience that we have?” And that’s really where we go off.

But for me, the signing out is way more crucial — leaving all that stuff at the theater, not taking my work home. There have been times when Travis and I will go out onstage when everyone’s left the theater, and you’re just left with the ghost light. We just thank the space because you never know what kind of portal is out there. We had [famous paranormal investigator] Adam Berry come in and do a ghost tour — that theater’s very haunted, and I don’t need any of those ghosts coming home with me. It’s not what I’m into. But we keep it fun.

Knight: Agreed. As the whole opening monologue is being said into the audience and the curtain is coming up, I’m standing on the other side of the front door waiting for my cue light to turn off. Everything up to that moment is exactly what Cher said — it’s light, there’s a lot of joking around. But the moment I’m putting that key in the door, it’s like all systems go. Especially in that first scene, because you see this couple at their best, and this is the only time in this play that you see them like that. So if I can enter that space with a sense of play, with a sense of wonder, with the goal of trying to make Cher laugh onstage — not Lou — or to surprise her in some way, that to me is so fun.
On their own feelings about horror:

Álvarez: It’s just not for me at all. If I’m going to watch a scary movie, it has to be at, like, 9 a.m. I still have time to recover. Being in it and acting in it is so different from actually watching it and choosing to be scared. I just am a naturally stressed person and have very high cortisol levels, and I would just prefer to stress out with my own thoughts.
Knight: I love horror. I’m a thrill-seeker in that regard.
Álvarez: He wanted to be a ghost hunter — like a legit ghost hunter.

Knight: I was obsessed with ghosts in my late teens, early 20s. We found this old home video, one of the last times I was at my parents’ house in Madison, Wisconsin. It was a video of me, and I had gotten this ghost book on Christmas morning. We were at my grandparents’ house, and I’m sitting next to my sister, and my grandma’s there, and I am explaining the difference between demons and ghosts and all these things as my sister just thousand-yard stares off into the distance — so annoyed that I’m talking about it.

Anyway, I love horror, and especially in October, it’s my jam to get on the streaming services and look at the horror section. I love that feeling of pressure in the chest, chill down the spine, wondering what’s going to happen next. There was a French television series called Marianne that scared the hell out of me last year when I watched it. I also did one of Levi Holloway’s first plays called Grey House in Chicago, and that was my first experience doing a horror stage play. During the whole rehearsal process, I was like, “What the hell are people going to think about this play?” That was my first taste of, like, “Oh, there’s an appetite for this thing.”
On memorable stage-door interactions:

Álvarez: To have two people with no names starring, headlining a show like this on Broadway has been really cool. People are seeing themselves represented onstage, which is really f*cking awesome and dope. Hearing young Latina women who are also in this industry say, “You’ve given me a dream role” — that’s a huge feat for me. That feels like I can die tomorrow, and I’m very happy with that.
Knight: I always get a kick when people are like, “I kept turning to my husband saying, ‘That’s how we talk to each other. That’s how we talk at home.’”

I’ve only had one sort of out-in-the-ether experience that I still think about. This person came to me and said, “This show deeply affected me. Could you sign this box?” And they handed me a small gift box that was empty. It was like a little cube, and I had the Sharpie that they give us at the stage door to sign Playbills. I was going to use that, and then they were like, “No, no, no, use mine.” I was about to write something, and then they said, “Can you write to Jimmy, and then something about demons or heroin?” I said, “Something about demons or heroin? What do you mean?” “Just anything, like bad things,” they said. So I wrote, “To Jimmy, demons, and heroin,” on this box, and I handed it back to them and they said, “Now I need you to sign your name.” So I took it back and kind of scribbled my name — but it wasn’t really my name because I was like, “What in the black magic is this?”

Álvarez: I just started watching New Girl again as a comfort show. You have to be so mindful of how you truly are using your energy when you’re doing a show — any show, but specifically this kind of show, eight times a week, is incredibly demanding. And we’ve all been sick this past week, so you just have to lock in and really take care of you.

It’s also when I feel like I can actually eat. We’ve just ran a marathon, so you feed yourself. And cereal is such a comfort food for me — you get the crunch, you get the sweet milk at the end. Ooh-wee. It’s a whole vibe, specifically the healthy version of Cinnamon Toast Crunch, but I’m sure Travis is pounding back 39 grams of protein or something, I don’t know.
Knight: No, usually 60 to 70 grams.

Knight: That’s the time of day I am eating half of my daily calories. I come home and eat and will watch something or play a video game called Helldivers 2 with two of my friends. And I try to be asleep before 1 a.m., but sometimes it’s tough.

Álvarez: I’m all about self-care, so I’m like, “Where can I get a massage? Who can touch my head? I need my pressure points.” And honestly, watching a movie on a Monday is like, the best for me. God, it restores my faith in humanity. The last thing I saw was that super crazy film with Hannah Einbinder and Gillian Anderson, Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma. I loved it. It was so f*cking weird. The simpler my Mondays are, the better, but you very rarely get that.

Knight: Laundry, grocery shopping. I mean, that’s just it. You pack it all in one day. The number of times I’m like, “It’s 4 o’clock already? F*ck.” I freak out about the time, because how does it go so fast?
On lessons learned from playing a married couple:
Knight: Jimmy has taught me that if you just stop and think for five seconds of your life before you speak, you could save yourself a tremendous amount of problems.
Álvarez: Have you applied it?
Álvarez: Oh. Well, let us know how it goes.
Knight: But truly, there is something to that. I don’t know, be more mindful, bro.
Álvarez: For me, it’s to be honest with the person who you’re going to share your life with. And also finding play, finding laughter within a relationship — that’s absolutely crucial.

items.title: Sorry, Victoria's Secret Angels—PINK Just Stole The Whole Show
items.description: All linked products are independently selected by our editors. If you purchase any of these products, we may earn a commission.
items.author: Alexis Bennett Parker
paragraphs: All linked products are independently selected by our editors. If you purchase any of these products, we may earn a commission.

I have a confession: Of all the things that happened at the 2026 Victoria's Secret Fashion Show, including a $50 million Fantasy Bra, it was a pair of sweatpants with charms dangling from the waistband that made me gag. Yes, sweatpants. And if you watched the PINK portion of Sunday night's show, you'll see exactly what I'm talking about.

There was a lot to take in. Oversized varsity jackets, leopard-print sweats, glittery little shorts, knee-high socks worn with heels, and enough sequins to make a Vegas showgirl jelly. It was giving early-2000s mall culture, the cool girl in your freshman dorm, and the version of me who used to spend an entire afternoon putting together an outfit just to go absolutely nowhere. In other words, I was obsessed.

Under the creative direction of Adam Selman, this year's Victoria's Secret Fashion Show traveled through the seasons, but PINK's Halftime Show took a detour into something refreshingly more playful. The looks were sporty, a little ridiculous (complimentary), and packed with the kind of styling details that made me reconsider what's already in my closet.

And here's the best part: Unlike some of the more elaborate runway creations, plenty of these pieces are actually shoppable. So, naturally, I went looking. Ahead, the PINK runway trends I can't stop thinking about and the pieces worth adding to your cart.

items.title: My Samsung’s Galaxy Watch9 For Kept Me Accountable
items.description: If you're like us, you've talked yourself out of a lot of good decisions, and into a few bad ones, because you couldn't tell what was actually worth it. VETTED is here to help. Whether it's a product, a procedure, or a place, we do the digging, ask the real qu
items.author: Sandy Pierre
paragraphs: If you're like us, you've talked yourself out of a lot of good decisions, and into a few bad ones, because you couldn't tell what was actually worth it. VETTED is here to help. Whether it's a product, a procedure, or a place, we do the digging, ask the real questions, and try it ourselves before we tell you a thing. If it made the cut, it's because it earned it.

I’m finally taking my fitness journey and my health seriously, and I’m learning that the best way to hold myself accountable is to actually track my progress. So when Samsung’s Galaxy Watch9 came out, I was interested in trying it for at least 30 days to see how if it could fit into my life and show me real-time results of how I was doing in my health journey.

The Galaxy Watch9 is Samsung’s smartwatch for tracking everyday activity, workouts, and sleep. It has a slim profile and feels very light on my wrist, which I appreciated while wearing it throughout the day.

In addition to fitness features, the watch offers wellness tools including Vitals and a Heart Health Score. For me, the appeal was having more information about my routine in one place, without needing to become a fitness expert to start paying attention.

My first order of business was tracking my steps. My personal goal was 10,000 a day, and being able to look at my wrist and see where I stood. I could easily check my progress throughout the day instead of guessing how much walking I’d done.

But then I found myself tracking more than that. I checked my daily activity, workouts, estimated calories burned, heart-related metrics, cycle, and sleep patterns. I went into the month focused on movement and ended up using the watch to keep tabs on more of my overall wellness.

I’m the type of person who needs to see progress to stay consistent. Having my activity right there on a screen gave me something tangible to check in with. The watch let me know when I hadn’t moved enough and offered encouragement when I was making progress.
I also appreciated that it picked up activities like jogging and swimming without me having to manually start tracking every time. That made it easier to focus on what I was doing.

I will admit, sometimes I wouldn’t wear it all the time. There were nights I forgot to put it on before bed and times I made it to the gym without it. Usually, I’d take it off because it didn’t go with my outfit or because I wanted to shower without it, then I'd forget to put it back on.
The Galaxy Watch9 starts at $379.99 for the Bluetooth model, with the price varying by size and connectivity. For the way I used it, I think it’s worth its value.

I’ve paid more for things I barely touched more than once. A watch that helps me keep up with goals I’m actively working toward feels easier to justify. The value, for me, comes from how often I reach for it and use the information it gives me.
Yes. While this watch was gifted, after 30 days of using it, I would spend my own money on it.

This was my introduction to being a Samsung girl, and I get the hype. I was impressed by how much information I could keep track of, just from my wrist. More than anything, it fit a need I already had: a way to see my activity and hold myself accountable as I work on being more consistent.

This watch makes sense for someone who likes seeing their progress, wants a digital accountability partner, or is figuring out how to make wellness a more regular part of their life. You don’t need to be training for a marathon to use this watch. I started with a daily step goal.
Phone compatibility matters, too. Check that your phone supports the watch and the features you want before buying; certain tools, including Vitals, require a compatible Samsung Galaxy phone.

For me, the Galaxy Watch9 is worth it. Over those 30 days, it made it easier to see what I was doing and where I needed to be more consistent. The movement reminders and automatic workout recognition were especially helpful because they gave me support without requiring me to manage every detail.

I’m still responsible for getting my steps in, going to the gym, and putting the watch back on after getting dressed, but having a way to track those efforts has been useful enough that I want to keep wearing it beyond the 30-day period.
I’m proud of myself for setting a challenge and sticking to it. Now, I’m already looking for new bands. If it’s going to be part of my daily routine, I want it to work with the outfit, too.

Sandy Pierre is the Branded Execution Manager at Refinery29 Unbothered and a contributing writer covering travel, lifestyle, and culture. When she’s not working on brand partnerships, she’s probably planning her next trip or curating a dinner for creatives in New York.

items.title: 20 Last-Minute Halloween Costumes On Amazon For All Your Spooky Plans
items.description: 20 Last-Minute Amazon Halloween Costumes For All Your Spooky Plans
items.author: Victoria Montalti
paragraphs: 20 Last-Minute Amazon Halloween Costumes For All Your Spooky Plans
(And you can, of course, re-create Prime Video's Off Campus costumes too!)
13 Going On 30's Jenna Rink

Amazon sells a dupe of Jenna Rink's iconic party dress from everyone's favorite coming-of-age movie 13 Going on 30, and we couldn't be more grateful for the last-minute costume inspo. This Y2K costume is perfect for nostalgic gals, and especially those turning 30 this year! Accessorize with some butterfly clips, a sweet baguette bag, strappy heels, and you're all set to dance to "Thriller" in style.

We've been seeing tons of amazing vintage clown makeup tutorials on our feeds in the lead-up to Halloween, so we had to include a retro clown costume to match. This black-and-white set is spooky and sexy, and even comes with the pom pom hat and striped tights for a full head-to-toe look. Just add face paint and transform into your clown character.

We're expecting lots of Dolly Parton tributes this Halloween for the late, great singer. And while you can throw together any sparkly Western tops with flared pants, we think the most important part of the look is the hair. Luckily, this voluminous blonde wig is available on Amazon as the cherry on top of your diva-approved look.
The Nightmare Before Christmas's Sally

Is it a Halloween movie? Is it a Christmas movie? Also yes. However you classify it, The Nightmare Before Christmas is a classic and Sally is an icon, making this a tried-and-true costume. We especially love this set because of the light blue bodysuit with scar details that replicates Sally's skin (without having to put on body paint all over!).
Off Campus' Allie Hayes As JLo

Okay, we're getting a little meta here. You're not dressing up as JLo, but rather as Off Campus' Allie Hayes dressed as JLo for her own Halloween party. While many dupes of the iconic Versace dress won't arrive before Halloween, this luxe dress is ready to ship on Amazon, and can be re-worn on your next summer vacation.
Off Campus' Dean Di Laurentis as Top Gun's Maverick

Every JLo needs her Maverick... right?! The ultimate couples costume this year will be Allie and Dean dancing in the Prime Video Off Campus Halloween party scene. And this jumpsuit is pretty true to Dean's costume. Wear it with your partner or bestie for the best pop culture reference. Add some aviator sunglasses and combat boots for the full effect.

She was a fairy! Or an elf fairy! This Halloween costume is particularly perfect for romantasy book readers. Pick your favorite boho dress and add on these enchanting wings, flower crown, magic wand, hair tinsel, and elf ears for the most cost-effective and simplest yet impactful look.
Knicks Fan (or Jordyn Woods... or Taylor Swift)

Knicks in five! The Knicks finally took home the 2026 NBA Championship, but before that it was total basketball fan mania last season. Everyone repped their Knicks merch, but if you don't have any yet, here's your chance to cart some up. And to make it even more pop culture-y, add Jordyn Woods's lucky orange handbag or Taylor Swift's kitschy "Stevie Knicks" T-shirt to complete your costume.

If you can't wait to hear "The Dead Dance" this season, you should probably dress as Wednesday Addams for Halloween. This costume kit mimics the Netflix series' viral black tulle dress with a Jenna Ortega-esque wig, black accessories, and even the Thing hand for an extra spooky touch. Even better, it costs under $50!
Zara Larsson's Midnight Sun Era

2026 was Zara Larsson's year as her Midnight Sun era catapulted her career and made us all fans. While you can truly wear your favorite swimsuits and coverups, it may be a bit too chilly, so we recommend a matching skirt set in a sunset ombre. Further get the Midnight Sun look with vibrant and sparkly makeup, like this bold glitter gel.

Another classic costume that you can't go wrong with. Dress as Little Red Riding Hood in this stunning under-$50 dress. To get the full effect, add a woven basket. And to win your costume contest, fill it with Halloween candy and hand it out at your house parties and bar crawls.

One of the biggest films of the year was undoubtedly Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey. While there aren't exact costume replicas of Athena, Calypso, or Queen Penelope, we think any Grecian goddess costume will get the point across, especially if you're paired with your Odysseus.
Pirate (or Renaissance Maiden)

We haven't had a good old-fashioned pirate movie in a while, and we're craving it. So consider dressing as a badass pirate for Halloween with this costume kit. It's not too kitschy and feels more upscale. And if you remove the eye patch, you can re-wear the outfit for a Renaissance fair!
Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader
Even if you're not a football fan, you may be a Dallas Cowboys Cheerleader fan, especially after binge-watching Netflix's America's Sweethearts documentary series.
Pick up your pom poms, slip into white cowboy boots and channel the DCC girls' "Thunderstruck" energy.

Sure, you can be a Disney princess, but dressing as a villain or sidekick is typically more fun to channel. And whether you love the original book or the movie remakes, the Mad Hatter is a character primed for Halloween. This top-rated Amazon costume gives you a quirky head-to-toe look, including a top hat, bow tie, and over-the-knee socks.

Picture it: You're dressed as Anxiety from Inside Out 2 while Doechii's "Anxiety" plays in the background of your TikTok video. Instantly iconic. The character we love to hate makes for a quirky and cute costume for all the anxious gals out there. Just add brown flared pants for the complete look.

When all else fails and you can't put together a totally unique Halloween costume, channel your spiritual and spooky senses, and be a witch. You can quite literally throw on any black dress (we personally like this corseted midi dress) and a pair of fall boots for an effortlessly chic look. Then, add this witch hat, choker, and mesh gloves for a total transformation.

Summer 2026 was defined by the World Cup and sporty style. But one person went beyond the field, and took over our feeds: Erling Haaland. The Norwegian Viking, um, we mean soccer player, became famous for his terrifying height and speed, but mostly for his luscious hair and signature man bun. So if you have long blonde hair, you simply have to do this costume. Add your soccer jersey and you have an easy, funny 'fit.

Spoiler: Fiyero turning into the scarecrow in Wicked: For Good was one of the biggest plot twists for those of us who didn't see the Broadway show. And since we won't have a third November in a row of Wicked mania, we're soaking up our favorite characters this Halloween. To make this a couples costume, have your bestie dress up as Cynthia Erivo's Elphaba and re-create the "As Long As You're Mine" scene!

items.title: Your Horoscope This Week: October 18 To 24
items.description: R29 babes, the week begins with the moon in Aquarius harmonizing with the final days of Libra Season, and there’s something refreshingly detached about the energy. Instead of getting pulled into every emotion, opinion, or little plot twist around you, you may
items.author: Dossé-Via Trenou
paragraphs: R29 babes, the week begins with the moon in Aquarius harmonizing with the final days of Libra Season, and there’s something refreshingly detached about the energy. Instead of getting pulled into every emotion, opinion, or little plot twist around you, you may find it easier to observe, stay present, and think more innovatively about the life you want to create next. Aquarius energy can help us zoom out without disconnecting completely, which is useful as we close out Libra Season and prepare to enter a much deeper emotional chapter.

On October 23rd, Scorpio Season begins and lasts for the next four weeks, immediately followed by Mercury retrograde in Scorpio on the 24th. That gives the start of spooky season a distinctly nostalgic undertone. Old conversations, people, habits, desires, or mindsets may circle back, but the point is to notice how differently you respond now. Scorpio Season is already introspective, and Mercury retrograde intensifies that tendency to revisit what has been buried or unfinished. Use the past as evidence of your growth, not an invitation to repeat the same cycle.

Then on October 25th, Venus retrograde leaves Scorpio after three intense weeks of shadow work and enters Libra, where Venus feels much more at home. The final stretch of the retrograde may feel noticeably lighter, especially in relationships, creativity, beauty, and the way we relate to pleasure. There’s still reflection happening, but the tone becomes less emotionally consuming and more focused on restoring harmony, reconnecting with what feels beautiful, and remembering that growth does not have to feel heavy all the time. It’s a welcome shift as we head toward next week’s Taurus Full Moon.
Read your horoscopes for your Sun and Rising signs for the most in-depth forecast.

Aries, the final days of Libra Season may help you see just how much your relationship patterns have been teaching you about yourself. With Venus retrograde in Scorpio happening in the background, partnership has probably felt less like a simple question of who you want around you and more like a mirror for deeper issues around trust, control, vulnerability, and reciprocity. You may have noticed where you rush to protect your independence, where you secretly want more reassurance, or where someone else’s behavior has been activating an older wound. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and pulls you even deeper into themes of intimacy, merging, shared resources, generational wealth, and emotional commitment. You may find yourself craving more depth than usual and becoming less interested in surface-level connections or half-hearted agreements.

Mercury retrograde begins in Scorpio on October 24th, intensifying that emotional depth with a strong return-to-the-past flavor. Old financial matters, trust issues, intimate conversations, or unresolved feelings may resurface, and the point is to understand what still has unfinished business rather than immediately reacting to it. Then on October 25th, Venus retrograde shifts back into Libra and returns the focus to partnership in a softer way. After weeks of Scorpio-level intensity, you may be ready to renegotiate, reconnect, or simply approach relationships with more grace and perspective. The weekend can feel like a reminder that intimacy works best when there’s both passion and peace.

Taurus, the final days of Libra Season may leave you thinking less about productivity and more about whether your daily life actually feels good to live inside of. With your ruler Venus retrograde in Scorpio throughout this stretch, routines, work, wellness, and boundaries may have become surprisingly emotional topics. You may have noticed how much your body reacts when a relationship feels off, how resentment creeps into your schedule, or where you have been over-functioning just to keep everything looking calm. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and turns the focus directly toward partnership, making you much more aware of who feels safe, reciprocal, and emotionally substantial enough to move forward with.

Mercury retrograde begins in Scorpio on October 24th, adding a strong review period around relationships, agreements, and conversations that may not have been fully resolved the first time. Someone from the past could resurface, or a current connection may need a second conversation with more honesty than before. Then on October 25th, Venus retrograde leaves Scorpio and returns to Libra, which may feel like a small exhale for you. The focus shifts back toward restoring balance in your routines and taking better care of your physical and emotional well-being, so by the weekend you may care less about figuring everyone else out and more about getting yourself back into alignment.

Gemini, the final days of Libra Season may remind you that pleasure is not supposed to become another task you optimize. Over the past few weeks, your romance, creativity, fun, and inner-child sector has been activated while Venus retrograded through Scorpio in the background, which may have made joy feel oddly entangled with work, health, responsibility, or emotional cleanup. You may have noticed that even when something exciting was happening, part of your brain was still making a spreadsheet about it. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and shifts your attention toward your routines, wellness, and daily responsibilities, encouraging you to take your energy more seriously and notice where your schedule has been helping or draining you.

Mercury, your ruler, stations retrograde in Scorpio on October 24th, so work patterns, health habits, unfinished tasks, or old responsibilities may need another pass before you can fully move forward. You could realize that a problem you thought was logistical is actually rooted in resentment, avoidance, or simple exhaustion. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, lightening the mood and redirecting some of your attention toward romance, creativity, and pleasure again. After all that Scorpio intensity, this can feel like the universe handing you back a little glitter and saying: “please remember you’re allowed to enjoy your life too.”

Cancer, the final days of Libra Season may help you see your home and emotional life with a little more honesty than usual. While Venus has been retrograde in Scorpio, questions around romance, pleasure, creativity, and emotional vulnerability may have quietly influenced the way you’ve been relating to family, privacy, and what “safe” really means. You may have noticed that certain people or environments bring out a more guarded version of you, while others make it easier to relax and feel like yourself. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and shifts the focus toward romance, creativity, pleasure, and inner-child healing, making the next few weeks feel more emotionally vivid and personally expressive.

Mercury retrograde begins in Scorpio on October 24th, adding a nostalgic layer to that part of your chart. An old crush, creative project, hobby, or desire may come back into focus, and you may find yourself asking why it mattered so much in the first place. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, redirecting your attention toward home, family, and emotional balance. After a week of digging through your heart a little, you may feel ready to make your private world softer, calmer, and more supportive of the version of you that’s trying to emerge.

Leo, the final days of Libra Season may show you just how much your environment and conversations have been shaping your mood lately. With Venus retrograde in Scorpio working through your home, family, and emotional-foundation zone, even casual exchanges may have felt more loaded than usual, especially if there were unspoken tensions underneath them. You may have learned that keeping the peace is not always the same thing as feeling at peace. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and pulls your attention inward, toward home, roots, privacy, and the parts of your life that need more protection, repair, or emotional honesty.

Mercury retrograde begins in Scorpio on October 24th, so old family conversations, living situations, memories, or private concerns may come back around for another look. This is less about getting dragged backward and more about understanding what still has a hold on you. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, lightening the emotional atmosphere and bringing more ease to communication, socializing, and your immediate surroundings. You may find it easier to say what you mean without turning every conversation into a courtroom drama, which, frankly, is a gift.

Virgo, the final days of Libra Season may leave you thinking differently about what actually makes you feel secure. Over the past few weeks, money, self-worth, and personal values have been highlighted while Venus retrograde in Scorpio stirred deeper questions around communication and the stories you tell yourself. You may have realized that some of your financial stress is tied to mental habits just as much as numbers, or that you have been undervaluing your time because you are too used to being the dependable one. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and shifts the focus more directly toward your mind, voice, learning, and immediate environment.

Mercury, your ruler, stations retrograde in Scorpio on October 24th, so conversations, paperwork, plans, or old thought patterns may need another round of attention. Something you said, heard, or decided earlier could look very different once you revisit it with more context. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, bringing the focus back toward money, pleasure, and self-worth in a softer way. You may feel more ready to reassess what is actually worth your time, your effort, and your coins — because being responsible doesn’t require permanently choosing the least enjoyable option.

Libra, the final days of your season may feel less like a victory lap and more like a quiet audit of what this past month actually taught you about yourself. With Venus retrograde in Scorpio putting pressure on money, self-worth, and security, your birthday season may have come with more reflection than usual around what you value, what you spend, and where you still look outside yourself for reassurance. You may be ending Libra Season with a clearer sense of which comforts genuinely support you and which ones have been disguising insecurity. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and shifts the spotlight more directly toward finances, resources, and the deeper question of what makes you feel materially and emotionally secure.

Mercury retrograde begins in Scorpio on October 24th, so old money decisions, pricing questions, purchases, or self-worth narratives may need another look before you move ahead. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into your sign, which changes the tone considerably. You may become more reflective about appearance, attraction, relationships, and how you want to present yourself, but there’s also something much softer about having your ruler back in Libra territory. Think of it as a chance to refine rather than reinvent: you may not need a whole new identity, just a more honest relationship with the one you already have.

Scorpio, this week has phoenix-rising-from-the-ashes energy written all over it. The final days of Libra Season may have felt like a strange in-between chapter, especially with Venus retrograde moving through your sign and forcing you to confront what you still want, what you have outgrown, and which version of yourself you are no longer interested in carrying forward. Then on October 23rd, the sun enters your sign, officially beginning your solar season. In a Fire Horse year and a 1 year in numerology, there’s something especially potent about this birthday season feeling like a true restart. Even with retrogrades swirling around you, you may feel more alive, more determined, and more willing to reclaim parts of yourself that got buried beneath the emotional heaviness of the past few weeks.

Then Mercury stations retrograde in Scorpio on October 24th, adding an interesting twist to this rebirth: the fresh start may come through remembering rather than rushing forward. Old ideas, conversations, ambitions, or versions of yourself may resurface and show you how much has changed since you first wanted them. You may realize that something you abandoned deserves another chance, or that a past identity no longer has enough power to pull you backward. And then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, moving some of the emotional processing into a more private, subconscious space. The spotlight is officially on you now, but part of your transformation is learning that you don’t have to drag every old wound onto the stage with you.

Sagittarius, the final days of Libra Season may leave you thinking more seriously about who still belongs in the future you’re building. Over the past few weeks, friendships, collaborations, and long-term goals have been highlighted while Venus retrograde in Scorpio quietly pulled you inward, making you more selective about where your energy goes. You may have realized that some social connections are inspiring you forward while others keep pulling you into old emotional patterns. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and shifts the mood into a much more private chapter, asking you to protect your energy, rest more intentionally, and make space for whatever’s been trying to surface beneath the noise.

Mercury stations retrograde in Scorpio on October 24th, and instead of simply making you “more introspective,” it may feel like your subconscious starts leaving little breadcrumbs everywhere. Dreams, memories, old fears, unfinished creative ideas, or even people you have not thought about in a while could start resurfacing with suspiciously good timing. Pay attention to what keeps returning; there may be something there worth understanding before you rush into your next big move. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, which can make the social energy feel lighter again and bring old friends, communities, or collaborations back into view. The vibe is less disappearing completely and more choosing your circle with much better discernment.

Capricorn, the final days of Libra Season may clarify which ambitions still feel worth the climb and which ones were built around someone else’s definition of success. Over the past few weeks, your career and public image have been highlighted while Venus retrograde in Scorpio quietly complicated the social side of things, making you more aware of who supports you, who competes with you, and which professional relationships actually feel reciprocal. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and shifts your attention toward friendship, community, collaboration, and the future you're trying to build beyond your résumé.

Mercury stations retrograde in Scorpio on October 24th, and this can make your social world feel like a reunion episode with unfinished plotlines. Old friends, former collaborators, abandoned goals, or group dynamics may resurface, but the interesting part is seeing them through the eyes of the person you are now. You may realize that a dream you once shelved still has life in it, or that a connection you thought was over simply needed diﬀerent boundaries. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, bringing your career and visibility back into focus with a softer edge. You may feel ready to refine how you present yourself professionally and choose opportunities that feel aligned with both your ambition and your peace.

Aquarius, the final days of Libra Season may help you see which beliefs, ambitions, or bigger-life plans still genuinely excite you and which ones you’ve simply been carrying out of habit. Over the past few weeks, travel, spirituality, and your broader worldview have been highlighted while Venus retrograde in Scorpio quietly stirred your career and reputation sector. You may have been asking bigger questions about whether the path you’re on actually reflects the person you’re becoming. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and turns the spotlight toward visibility, ambition, and the legacy you want to build.

Mercury stations retrograde in Scorpio on October 24th, but rather than just repeating the same career themes, this can feel like an opportunity to revise the story people know you by. An old professional idea, former collaborator, past ambition, or unfinished public project may come back into circulation, and you may suddenly understand how it could be approached differently now. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, bringing a little more air and perspective back into the picture. You may feel ready to reconnect with travel, learning, or a wider vision of your future, which can be exactly what helps you remember why you’re working so hard in the first place.

Pisces, the final days of Libra Season may leave you with a clearer sense of what intimacy, trust, and emotional reciprocity actually require from you now. Over the past few weeks, shared resources, merging, vulnerability, and deeper emotional bonds have been highlighted while Venus retrograde in Scorpio kept pulling bigger questions about meaning, faith, travel, and your future into the background. You may have realized that who you trust is closely connected to what you believe about yourself and where your life is headed. Then Scorpio Season begins on October 23rd and shifts the focus toward expansion, perspective, education, spirituality, and experiences that help you feel more connected to something larger than your current circumstances.

Mercury stations retrograde in Scorpio on October 24th, and this may feel less like “going backward” and more like reopening a door you were too busy or uncertain to walk through the first time. An old travel plan, course of study, spiritual practice, or long-distance connection could return with new relevance, especially if it still feels unfinished. Then the week ends with Venus retrograde shifting into Libra, bringing your attention back toward intimacy, trust, and shared resources in a softer, more balanced way. You may feel ready to have honest conversations about what you need from others and what you’re genuinely willing to share in return.

items.title: Everything We Know About The Fourth Wing TV Series So Far
items.description: Since landing on bookshelves in May 2023, Fourth Wing — the debut novel in Rebecca Yarros’ The Empyrean series — has taken the world of romantasy to unprecedented heights, catapulting the genre into a global phenomenon. Set in the fictional, highly militarized
items.author: Ella Taverner; Kathleen Newman-Bremang
paragraphs: Since landing on bookshelves in May 2023, Fourth Wing — the debut novel in Rebecca Yarros’ The Empyrean series — has taken the world of romantasy to unprecedented heights, catapulting the genre into a global phenomenon. Set in the fictional, highly militarized kingdom of Navarre, the novel charts the perilous, emotionally charged journey of Violet Sorrengail, a scribe-turned-dragonrider, as she navigates her newfound place at the prestigious Basgiath War College. With relentless action, horny high-stakes intrigue, and a generous dose of steam, it’s no surprise that Fourth Wing broke publishing records and established itself as a staple on the New York Times Bestseller list. Since then, Yarros has released two follow-up books in the series — Iron Flame and Onyx Storm — which have only strengthened The Empyrean saga’s chokehold on romantasy fans worldwide. A Michael B. Jordan produced adaptation of the series has been announced and now, it has its stars. It has been reported that Esther McGregor (you may know her from We Were Liars or as Ewan's daughter) and Emilio Sakraya (best known for Warrior Nun) have been cast as Violet Sorrengail and  Xaden Riorson, respectively.
With confirmation that Fourth Wing will be filling our screens in the not-so-distant future, here’s everything we know about the TV series so far.

For the uninitiated, Fourth Wing is the first novel in Rebecca Yarros' drama-filled romantasy series, The Empyrean. The story follows 20-year-old Violet Sorrengail as she embarks on her first year at the prestigious and unforgiving Basgiath War College, forced to leave her quiet life as a scribe at her mother’s command. Her mother, a powerful General in the Navarre military, insists Violet follow in her siblings’ footsteps and become a dragon rider — despite her physical fragility (she suffers from Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome, much like author Rebecca Yarros) and lack of preparation for the brutal demands of the Riders Quadrant. At Basgiath, Violet initially finds protection under the wing of her loyal childhood best friend Dain Aetos, but is soon entangled in a charged enemies-to-lovers dynamic with the brooding and ruthless wing leader, Xaden Riorson. With fierce hand-to-hand combat, daring dragon trials, and danger at every turn, the story blends romance, action, and survival.

The TV adaptation of Fourth Wing is being produced by Amazon MGM Studios in collaboration with Michael B. Jordan’s production company, Outlier Society. At the time of writing, no filming date or release date has been announced, though in an interview with Deadline in January 2026, Jordan confirmed the adaptation is “coming" and at the annual Amazon MGM Studios Upfront presentation in New York City this month, the studio announced the series order for the adaptation.
Yarros has also confessed she has already read some versions of the pilot script, a positive indication that the pre-production ball is rolling.

Michael B. Jordan is about a decade too old to play Xaden Riorson himself so he cast the next best thing (we're joking! Relax, Booktok!). Based on the source material, we knew that Xaden definitely wouldn't be white. After the plethora of casting theories flying around social media as to who should play protagonist Violet Sorrengail and her love interest, we now have our answer.

All the major outlets (Deadline, Variety, etc) are reporting that Esther McGregor has been cast in the role of Violet Sorrengail and Emilio Sakraya will play Xaden Riorson. Amazon Prime Video, the studio distributing the series, has yet to confirm the news but it's looking like these two are locked. As usual, the fan reaction has been mixed but we think these two look like the perfect Xaden and Violet.

The casting comes after Yarros made one promise to fans: Xaden would be played by a person of color. Speaking to Variety in November 2023, the author said, "We’re just going to say he’s POC; we’re just going to leave it at that. I didn’t rise to the bait of a lot of those [fan] posts, which I think probably got me some flak, but I knew we were already in development for TV, and I want to make sure that role is open to as much diversity as possible. So I was never going to give the readers my vision because I know that once you give the readers your vision, that’s what they’re gonna stick to. And I wanted to make sure we left it open to as much diversity as possible."

Given the huge world-building requirements (see: dragons) for the adaptation, the production is probably going to be a long one. And since the casting was just announced, there is no official trailer for Fourth Wing yet.
As we learn more developments about the production of Fourth Wing, we'll be sure to update this article.

items.title: How to overcome task paralysis | Psyche Guides
items.description: is a licensed clinical psychotherapist, board-certified coach, and ADHD-certified clinical services provider. He teaches psychology at Southern New Hampshire University, US.
items.author: Joe Wilner
paragraphs: is a licensed clinical psychotherapist, board-certified coach, and ADHD-certified clinical services provider. He teaches psychology at Southern New Hampshire University, US.
is a licensed clinical psychotherapist, board-certified coach, and ADHD-certified clinical services provider. He teaches psychology at Southern New Hampshire University, US.

It’s Thursday afternoon and the report has been sitting unfinished since Tuesday. Not untouched. You’ve opened it and closed it four or five times now, but can’t seem to make any progress. There’s also the dental appointment you’ve been meaning to schedule since January, and the email you finished writing last week that’s still sitting in your drafts for some unnameable reason.

You’re not procrastinating as such, because that’s a choice – like when you put off the tax return to watch the game, knowing at some level that you’re trading tomorrow’s stress for tonight’s comfort. This is about situations that run the other way. You want to start. You’ve cleared the afternoon, closed the distracting tabs on your screen, told yourself today is the day, and still nothing moves.

That strange bind, being unable to begin something you genuinely want to do, is task paralysis. I’ve spent years as a therapist working with adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), who often experience this problem because of their difficulties with executive function – the ability to plan and execute tasks. But it’s not just people with ADHD who struggle in this way. Push anyone through enough stress, too little sleep, or too far past their limits, and the same executive function system can start to falter, causing task paralysis to set in.

For many of my clients with ADHD, the usual support tools like task planners rarely seemed to help. When I learned about goal management training (GMT), an evidence-based programme for strengthening executive function, it stood out right away as something different. It offered a toolkit with an actual sequence of steps and specific strategies for building relevant skills. I trained in GMT, worked it into my clinical sessions, and watched it help people finally bridge the gap between knowing what they want to do and doing it.

GMT originated in the 1990s, when the psychologist Ian Robertson developed it at Cambridge University for people recovering from brain injury, whose capacity to hold a goal and act on it had been compromised. They would know that a goal mattered, hold it in mind, and yet still drift the moment something more immediate tugged at them. Robertson later refined the approach with the neuroscientist Brian Levine, and the version clinicians use today grew out of their collaboration.

Whether you have ADHD or you’re struggling for other reasons, I’ve written this Guide to show you how to use GMT to help yourself. The approach includes four stages: stop, define the goal, list the steps, check (repeated as needed). I’ll explain each of these stages in turn, then add three more that I’ve come to rely on with clients. None of the stages are complicated on their own. What makes them work is repetition: the executive functions you’re leaning on can even get stronger the more you use them.

As you read through the steps, I suggest you keep one stuck task in your mind, whether it’s that unfinished report, the unsent email, or something else, and that you try putting each step to work on it.

Task paralysis is not the same as procrastination. You want to start now and you know what needs doing, but you just can’t get going. It’s common in ADHD, but stress or too little sleep can cause it in anyone.
Goal management training offers a toolkit for overcoming task paralysis. It runs in four stages – stop, define the goal, list the steps, check – repeated as needed. This Guide adds three more.

Pause and regulate before you act. A few slow breaths or a quick stretch will help you think more clearly and catch when you’re drifting into autopilot. Give the pause a built-in ending so it doesn’t turn into a long break.
Keep your goal in mind. Intentions can fade fast unless you rehearse them. Keep repeating your goal to yourself in your head so that you stay on track.
Take the next smallest step. Shrink the first move until starting costs almost nothing. If naming the step makes you sigh, it isn’t small enough.

Check your work against the goal. Halfway through and at the end, ask: Am I doing what I meant to? If you’ve drifted, go back to the pause and start the cycle again, or take the next smallest step you can.
Make time visible. Use alarms and timers to keep time in view. Label an alarm with the action that gets you started, such as ‘open report, read last paragraph’.

Borrow structure from other people. ‘Body doubling’ is working alongside someone else in person or over video, and many people with ADHD say it helps. Try this: twice a week, get on a video call with someone grinding through their own backlog.

Build a ritual. Start work with the same setup each time so that it becomes your cue to begin. Keep it simple: often one element, like sitting in a specific chair or turning your timer to face you, is the most important cue.
Pause and regulate before you act

An important part of the brain for planning and self-regulation is the prefrontal cortex. The Yale neuroscientist Amy Arnsten studies what happens to this brain region under pressure, and her findings show that even mild stress can produce measurable losses in working memory, attention, and the ability to think flexibly.

This is where GMT starts, and it asks you to do the opposite of what your instinct might be telling you. Instead of pushing harder to force your way into the task, it’s better to regulate your stress levels first. Before you plan, before you organise, before you try to concentrate, just pause. That pause provides the foundation for the remaining steps and trains you to catch the point where your attention has drifted off the task and onto autopilot. The better you get at this, the more likely you’ll be able to intervene and get back to where you meant to be.

To reset after the pause, keep it simple and physical: a few slow exhales, a walk to the window and back, a long stretch, or a roll of the shoulders. Almost everyone balks at this because they worry they won’t get back on track. Whatever you pick, give it a built-in ending. One project manager told me her breaks had a way of turning into 40 minutes, so we picked a pause that ends on its own: three exhales, counted on her fingers.

Imagine you head upstairs to grab your laptop and collect the laundry. On the way, your child calls out from the bathroom, you help them, and 10 minutes later you’re back at your desk without the laptop, the laundry still sitting wet in the machine. Both things were right there in your mind minutes ago. Now they’re gone.

Working memory is where you hold the information you need right now, and that includes your intentions, such as going to fetch the laptop. Unfortunately, it’s fragile and limited in what it can store.

That’s why the skill you’re training in this step is keeping your goal in mind and coming back to it, before it has a chance to decay. GMT uses the image of a mental blackboard, a place where the one thing you’re trying to do stays posted, so you can keep glancing back at it instead of trusting it to survive on its own in a crowded head.

So, on your next trip upstairs for the laptop and laundry, you keep repeating the intention: laptop, laundry. Two words, held in mind. Your child still calls out, and you stop to help, but the words are waiting when you’re done. You grab the laptop, collect the laundry, and come back down with both.
Take the next smallest step

Once the goal is in mind, you still have to take action. It’s the apparent scale of the task that often causes problems here. Shrinking the task will help. Make the first move small enough that starting costs you almost nothing.

Take the example of making that dental appointment. The first step isn’t to schedule it. Half the reason it’s sat there since January is that ‘schedule it’ is code for a whole daunting chain: find the number, check the calendar, endure the hold music, commit to a date. So, break the task into mini steps and aim to complete the very first one – give yourself permission to stop there to ensure it feels truly doable. In this example, find the number and write a note. If you get that far and you still have momentum, great – you can proceed to the next step. If not, the good thing is you’ve started the process and tomorrow you can take it further.

People rarely shrink tasks enough. A graduate student offered ‘open the document and write one sentence’ as her smallest possible move for finishing an assignment. She stayed stuck for another two weeks because the sentence was the hard part. Opening the file and reading her previous paragraph was the step that ultimately got her started. My rule of thumb now: if naming the step makes you sigh, it isn’t small enough.
Check your work against the goal

One small step is progress only if another follows it. Checking, the fourth stage in GMT, is what turns finding the dentist’s number into an appointment in the calendar. Checking means holding what you are doing up against what you said you would do, and it happens at two points.

Roughly halfway through, you ask: Am I still doing the thing I said I’d do? And, at the end of a work block: Is this the thing I meant to make? One client looked up at a check-in and found he’d spent 25 minutes reformatting the headings of a report he hadn’t started writing. He took it as proof he was hopeless. I took it as the ‘check’ doing its job. Without it, he’d have reformatted until 5 pm and called it a day’s work.

That reaction is common. People hear ‘check’ and reach for a verdict: Am I doing enough?Have I wasted the morning? Those questions stop the work cold. The useful question is smaller: Am I doing what I meant to do? It takes a second to answer, and it points you towards the task instead of back at yourself. If you’ve gone off track, reset by returning to this Guide’s first stage and restarting the cycle.

Asking is easy. Remembering to ask is the hard part, since forgetting is the whole problem. So pair the halfway check with something that happens anyway: a timer, a finished cup of coffee, the walk back from the bathroom.

Then close the loop. Every work block ends one of two ways: the task is done and you’ve achieved what you wanted, or there’s more to do – so you name the next smallest step and decide when you’ll take it. Write it where you’ll see it, or you’ll be trusting the same memory that lost the goal in the first place.
The four stages I’ve described so far belong together and run in order. This step and the two that follow are more like supports that you can reach for as needed.

The clinical psychologist Russell Barkley describes ADHD as a kind of ‘time blindness’, and clinicians often put it more simply: the ADHD brain lives in two time zones, ‘now’ and ‘not now’. A deadline three weeks out sits in ‘not now’, weightless and theoretical, until it lurches into ‘now’ somewhere around midnight the night before.

If that sounds like you, one antidote is to use external cues as much as possible, to move time out into the open where you can see it or hear it. For instance, an alarm labelled ‘start the report’ rather than ‘submit the report’ aims at the real sticking point, which is remembering and starting. Clients taught me to go further and name the specific action, because ‘report’ is easy to swipe away at nine in the morning, while ‘open report, read last paragraph’ is harder to argue with when you can picture yourself doing it. If you want to work for a given amount of time, set a countdown timer on your desk (or a virtual one on your screen).
Borrow structure from other people

One of the odder observations in ADHD research is that people who find it hard to get started alone often work noticeably better with someone else in the room. ‘Body doubling’ – working alongside someone else in person or over video – has spread through ADHD communities because so many people find it helps. The strange part is how little the other person has to do. No accountability, no conversation, no sense of being watched. All it takes is a shared table at the library, a co-working space, or a video call with a friend who’s heads-down on their own work.

You can use this to your advantage. Let’s say you’re struggling to write that report. Try this: twice a week, get on a video call with someone grinding through their own backlog. Say hello, name what you’re each about to start, then mute and work. You might find that just having another person on screen, head down, is enough to ease you into a task you’ve been dodging for days.

If your process is working, repeat it. Sit in the same chair at the same hour with the same coffee before you work, and your brain starts to read that setup as the signal to go. The context becomes the cue. Give it a few weeks and the ritual starts to run itself: same chair, timer turned to face you, coffee on your right, the choice to begin already made before you sit down.

Keep it simple. The risk is that a ritual grows out of control, to the point where you need the right desk, the right hour, and the right playlist. Then a work trip or a sick child takes all three away and your ability to work goes with them. But one element is usually doing the real signalling, and it’s smaller than you’d think. For one of my clients it was the chair and the view out of the window. For another it was nothing but turning the timer to face her. Identify that element and you may find you can start almost anywhere.
